title: The Capex Correction Continues
text:
The Capex Correction Continues

Thomas Gatley

Gavekal Dragonomics | 9 Sep 2026

After years of rapid investment growth, listed Chinese companies started to dial back their capital expenditures around 2024 (see Manufacturing Investment Is Rationalizing). That investment restraint is continuing in 2026, a result of lackluster domestic demand, slim margins, tighter access to equity-market financing and somewhat more restrained industrial-policy support. While corporate profits are up, those gains are largely confined to electronics and commodities firms. For the vast majority of Chinese companies, persistently weak domestic demand means they will probably continue to limit their capex through the next year and beyond. That caution on investment means that China’s excess capacity problems should no longer be worsening, as current rates of investment are only enough to offset depreciation and are not adding to total capacity.
